text:
Alex R: quick heads-up — sawtooth oscillation in continuous-batcher queue on gpu-pool-3. p95 stable (~120ms) but p99 spikes to ~480ms every ~10–12s window after yesterday's kernel-selection merge.
Maria T: saw the same on dashboard. spikes line up with max_wait_ms timer firing. looks like batching timer + kernel fallback cadence.
Sanjay P: can you paste the sched logs / microbatch traces? especially around the spike window.
Alex R: putting a small extract. Note: timestamps are relative.
```
[batcher] enqueue req id=0x7f3 len=32 tokens
[batcher] formed microbatch size=4 tokens=128 delay=11ms
[kernel] selecting kernel=fast_attn_seq32 -> compiled
[kernel] switch cost ~28ms
[serve] start token stream -> kv-hit=0.73
[batcher] flush due to max_wait_ms=10
```
Lee: interesting — kernel switch cost ~28-30ms is non-trivial. if several requests trigger fallback around the same time we add extra tail.
Maria T: i ran a quick ablation: set max_wait_ms 10->6 and max_batch_tokens 2048->4096. p99 dropped 480->260ms, p95 rose slightly 120->135ms. kv-cache hit rate dropped ~5% because longer batches push more unique prefixes.
Alex R: yea, tradeoff. shorter wait reduces KV reuse but avoids kernel churn. we saw CPU burn increase ~12% with lower max_wait_ms.
Sanjay P: what about limiting kernel fallback? prefer stable kernel for seq_len<=64 and force single kernel path.
Alex R: tried that in infra-branch: forced-kernel-for-short-seq path cuts kernel-switch events by 80%. p99 drops further to ~220ms, but we saw some quality regression on bench prompts (different attention impl subtle FP differences).
CI Bot: perf test run id=ci/2026-03-12-88: p99 before=478ms after-force=222ms, accuracy-diff=+0.2% on evalset
Maria T: accuracy change minor, but need sign-off from ML.
Lee: propose AB: group A=default, B=force-single-kernel, run 24h window on canary pool. monitor p99, kv-hit, and RL evals.
Sanjay P: also want to try Adaptive max_wait: increase during low qps, shrink when qps spiky. simple PID on queue length.
Alex R: sketch for config
```
{"batcher": {"max_wait_ms": 10, "max_batch_tokens": 2048, "adaptive_wait": true}}
```
Maria T: note that enabling adaptive_wait interacts badly with queue-oscillation if step-size too large -> saw oscillatory behavior. tune with damping factor.
Lee: action items:
- run AB canary for force-single-kernel (Alex)
- run AB for adaptive_wait with conservative damping (Maria)
- add a dashboard for kernel-switch events and microbatch size distribution (Sanjay)
- ping ML for eval sign-off (Lee)
Alex R: I'll post experiment configs and a short profiler flame snippet later. thanks :thumbsup:
Maria T: TY. posting dashboard link: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/expr/1912345678 :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Sanjay P: I'll add alerts for p99>300ms and kernel-switch-rate>5/s
Lee: cool. if we hit regressions rollback to previous kernel-selection commit and set max_wait_ms=12 temporarily.
Alex R: agreed, keeping run short and observable. will update here with results.
